title: What you already do
hookLine: you have a practice already, whether you call it one or not: Nanquan says ordinary mind is the Way, and Zhaozhou pushes back
tomorrow: a prince's father hid every old and sick face. what got past the wall?

cards: Coffee on the back step every morning, the same mug, the same five minutes of watching the street. Is that a practice, or just caffeine? Zen has an old argument about exactly this, between a teacher and his student.
The student, Zhaozhou, asks his teacher Nanquan: what is the Way? And Nanquan gives an answer that sounds almost too easy. Ordinary mind is the Way.
Your coffee, in other words, might already count. But Zhaozhou isn't satisfied, and his pushback is the real puzzle.

teach.h: IF YOU AIM AT IT, YOU TURN AWAY.
teach.b: Should I aim at it, then? Zhaozhou asks. If you aim at it, says Nanquan, you turn away from it.

teach.h: HOW WILL I KNOW IT'S THE WAY?
teach.b: If I don't aim at it, how will I know it's the Way? Let both views speak. Nanquan's side: the Way isn't somewhere else, waiting behind a special technique.
It's in washing a bowl and walking to work. Chase it as something extra and you've already split your life in two. Zhaozhou's side, and it's strong: if everything already counts, nothing does.
A habit you never notice is just a habit. How would you know? Nanquan's answer goes past both.
The Way, he says, isn't a matter of knowing or not knowing. Knowing is a kind of illusion, and not knowing is just blankness. Reach it without doubt, and it's open and wide as the sky.
The story says Zhaozhou woke up right there. Here's the teaching Zen draws from it: practice isn't only what happens on the cushion.
Ordinary mind, awake in ordinary things, is the Way itself. Zen monasteries treat cooking and cleaning as practice too. So your coffee isn't nothing.
It's already here. What it lacks, maybe, is you, awake in it.

how: Zen students study this exchange as case 19 of the Gateless Gate, and Zen monasteries treat daily work, cooking, cleaning and gardening, as part of practice alongside sitting.

games.q: what does “what you already do” mean?
o: everything you do wrong that a practice has to fix
a new routine you add on top of your usual day
the habits you already keep, which can already be practice

games.q: Nanquan and Zhaozhou: tap the pairs.

s: in Zen, practice happens only while sitting in meditation
Nanquan says ordinary mind is the Way, and monasteries treat work as practice too.
Zhaozhou questioned his teacher's answer before he understood it
he asked: if I don't aim at it, how will I know it's the Way?

games.q: Ray says Zoe's morning coffee already counts as practice; Inés says it's just caffeine. before siding with Ray, what's the strongest case for Inés?
o: Zhaozhou's: if everything counts and you never notice it, how would you know?
coffee can't be spiritual, because it's a stimulant.
only practices taught by a teacher can ever count.
games.why: Zhaozhou pushed back on 'ordinary mind is the Way' with exactly that question. Nanquan's answer: the Way is past knowing and not knowing, and it's right here.

practice: Walk slowly through your home and stop at each place where you already do something every day: the kettle, the sink, the window, the door. At each one, name the habit silently, as if it were already practice. It might be.

wordCard.voice: What you already do: the habits that are already a practice, in Nanquan's words ordinary mind, waiting for you to be awake in them.

orig.note: Chinese: ordinary mind is the Way, Nanquan's answer to Zhaozhou.

carryVoice: Keep this one: already here, the Way in the ordinary, if you're awake to it. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Wumenguan (The Gateless Gate), case 19: 'Ordinary mind is the Way' (Nanquan and Zhaozhou)
